claims.text: A DFT-ML framework using phonon dispersions and microstructural descriptors will accurately identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys.
Atomic mass variance, lattice distortion, grain-boundary energy, and sensitivity-selected microstructural descriptors are predictive of phonon thermal conductivity.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is single phase.
Doping CoCrFeMnNi with a few atomic percent Al or Cu is isovalent doping that can tune atomic-size mismatch.
Sensitivity analysis can identify additional useful descriptors such as stacking-fault density and nanoprecipitate distribution.
Severe plastic deformation followed by ultra-high-vacuum annealing will produce 20–50 nm grains in CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys.
The specified processing will yield oxidation-free microstructures.
The intervention will increase atomic-scale lattice distortion.
The intervention will create high densities of nanocrystalline grain boundaries and stacking faults.
Lattice distortion and strain fluctuations strengthen phonon scattering and reduce lattice thermal conductivity.
Stacking faults act as effective phonon-scattering centers.
Nanoprecipitates can scatter low-frequency phonons.
Lattice distortions and nanoscale grain boundaries together scatter phonons over the full frequency range.
The selected descriptors will allow the model to identify compositions with greatly reduced phonon mean free paths.
A reduced phonon mean free path will lead to lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Selected alloys will show at least a 20% reduction in phonon thermal conductivity relative to conventional CALPHAD-based predictions.
Selected alloys can attain room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity below 0.1 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹.
Conventional CALPHAD and binary-phase-diagram methods do not incorporate detailed microstructural descriptors.
The approach is limited to single-phase, oxidation-free, nanograined CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys and may not extend to multiphase, oxidized, or microstructurally uncontrolled materials.
Consistently exceeding 0.1 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ at room temperature or failing to achieve the predicted 20% reduction would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The target conductivity is described as intrinsically low, but much of the proposed reduction is attributed to processing-dependent grain boundaries, stacking faults, and precipitates, which are extrinsic microstructural effects.

The scope is restricted to single-phase alloys, while nanoprecipitate distribution is proposed as a model descriptor and experimental microstructural feature; a substantial precipitate population would generally imply a multiphase microstructure.
